chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Sa'd ibn Abi Amr al-Jallab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

He said to the wife of Sa'd: 'Congratulations to you, O Khansa'a! So even if Allah did not give you anything except your daughter, Umm al-Husayn, Allah would have given you abundant goodness. Indeed, the example of a righteous woman among women is like the example of the 'Asam crow among crows, and it is the one with a white leg.'

key_terms.أُمَّ الْحُسَيْنِ: Umm al-Husayn (Mother of Husayn), a title often referring to Fatimah al-Ma'sumah or a specific daughter in this context
key_terms.الْغُرَابِ الْأَعْصَمِ: The 'Asam crow (literally 'the one with the white leg'), used here as a metaphor for rarity and distinctiveness
key_terms.الْغِرْبَانِ: The crows (plural of crow), representing the common or ordinary

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor used in Shia hadith to describe the rarity of a righteous woman?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the exceptional virtue of Umm al-Husayn by comparing her to the 'Asam crow—a rare white-legged crow—emphasizing that righteousness is scarce among women. This metaphor underscores the high spiritual status of virtuous women in Shia tradition, suggesting that even a single righteous daughter constitutes a profound divine blessing. The narration serves as both a commendation of specific lineage and a general principle regarding the rarity of female piety.

en.hubeali: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Sa’ad Bin Abu Amro Al Jallab,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said to the wife of Sa’ad: ‘Congratulations to you, O Khansa’a! So even if Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not Give you anything except for your daughter, Umm Al-Husayn, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would have (still) Given you abundant goodness. But rather, the example of a righteous woman among the women is like the example of the ‘Chough’ crow among the crows, and it is white in one of its legs’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Sa‘d ibn abu “Amr al-Jallab who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to the wife of Sa‘d, ‘How fortunate it is for you O Khansa’, if Allah will not give you anything else besides your daughter, mother of al-Husayn; still Allah has given you a great deal of good. The case of a virtuous woman among women is like an al- A‘sam crow among the crows. It is the one which has one white leg.’”
